questions.q: What real problem does parameterizing a linked service solve?
options: Avoiding building a nearly-identical linked service for every database/value that differs only in one detail
It makes a linked service run faster
It removes the need for a linked service entirely
It automatically encrypts all data in transit
questions.explain: Without parameters, connecting to fifty near-identical databases means building fifty separate linked services. Parameterizing lets one linked service serve all fifty, with the actual value supplied at run time.

questions.q: Where do you find the option to parameterize a field in the Studio UI?
options: The "Add dynamic content" link underneath a configurable field
The Monitor hub's Alerts tab
A separate "Parameters" application outside Data Factory Studio
Only by editing the ARM template after publishing
questions.explain: Any field that supports parameterization shows an "Add dynamic content" link beneath it, opening an expression editor.

questions.q: What does the expression @{linkedService().DBName} actually do?
options: Reads the linked service's own DBName parameter value at run time
Permanently hard-codes the database name to "DBName"
Deletes the DBName parameter
Only works inside a dataset, never inside a linked service
questions.explain: This expression pulls in whatever value was actually passed for the DBName parameter when the linked service was used, rather than a fixed value.

questions.q: According to Microsoft's own guidance, what should you never do with a password or secret?
options: Parameterize it directly — store it in Azure Key Vault and parameterize the secret's name instead
Use it in a linked service at all
Store it anywhere other than plain text in the JSON
Reference it more than once across different linked services
questions.explain: A parameter is visible in plain text wherever it's set. Secrets belong in Azure Key Vault, with only the secret's name parameterized — never the secret's actual value.

questions.q: What happens if a connector doesn't offer the built-in "Add dynamic content" experience?
options: You can still parameterize it by hand, via Advanced → Specify dynamic contents in JSON format
That connector can never be parameterized under any circumstances
You must switch to a completely different connector
Parameterization only works for Azure Blob Storage and Azure SQL Database
questions.explain: Every linked service type supports parameterization — connectors without the native UI experience can still be parameterized by writing the JSON directly under Advanced settings.
